title: A flood, then quiet years
hook: Would flood-insurance demand stay high as the event recedes?

knows: basic arithmetic and reading a small table
doesNotKnow: Distinguish the recent-event response from longer-run decay in attention.

misconception: The quantities in this case can be combined without checking their reference, denominator, or information boundary.
objective: Distinguish the recent-event response from longer-run decay in attention.
keyState: Both complete computed cases are visible as retained observations; the question-case picture survives Reset.

claims.text: A toy attention response begins nine percentage points above baseline and retains 70% each year. After one year, what remains? Toy inputs A=[9, 0.7]; B=[9, 1].
claims.source: Local explicit hypothetical assumptions in spec.ts and model.ts; not participant measurements.

claims.text: Computed results: [[9, 6.3, 0.25422772409999983], [9, 9, 9]]. Labels: Year 0 pp, Year 1 pp, Year 10 pp.
claims.source: compute() in the lesson-local model.ts; finite numeric operations over the explicit inputs.

claims.text: The declining path separates a recent-event spike from its persistence. The comparison holds attention constant instead. Extrapolating the immediate response requires a retention assumption; the toy rate is not an estimate of a real community’s insurance choices.
claims.source: The two controlled cases in spec.ts; scope limited to these toy inputs and displayed model rule.

claims.text: A new toy case uses Initial rise pp=9, Retention/year=1. What is Year 1 pp? Answer: 9.
claims.source: compute() applied to the contrasting new input case; source list is an idea pointer only.

recall.question: A new toy case uses Initial rise pp=9, Retention/year=1. What is Year 1 pp?
recall.why: Applying the stated toy rule to the new inputs gives 9. The result depends on these assumptions; it is not a universal behavioral response.

sourceProvenance.text: Flood insurance take-up rises about 9% the year after a local flood, then falls back to baseline over roughly a decade (Gallagher, 2014).
sourceProvenance.caveat: Original list says figures are approximate and papers were not individually rechecked. No empirical source is verified by this build.

meaningfulDifference: Distinguish the recent-event response from longer-run decay in attention.
